correctness.rationale: The result models each contiguous binary trigram abc as an arc ab->bc in the order-two de Bruijn digraph; identical arc copies are indistinguishable. A published proper-transposition uniqueness test is specialized to a finite deterministic automaton, with an extra endpoint/rotation rejection for unanchored linear profiles. Rebuilt the 166 reachable states and transitions independently from the source algorithm; checked each of 166 integer coordinates of r45-3r33+3r21-r9=0. Right multiplication by M^k proves the third period-12 finite-difference identity for all n>=9, and exact 3x12 seed values give the displayed quadratic residues. Brute-force enumerated all 2^n strings and grouped by full trigram histogram through n=16; counts match 3..16. General uniqueness characterization is taken from cited Euler-trail theory, not inferred from sample tests.

This finite-alphabet result remains mathematically interesting without extending to noisy higher alphabets.
